label: AI-written, unbriefed: a fresh agent given only each task's template, its checker and 20 dev examples

prompts.gsm8k: For this task, show short working before the answer. First state in a few words exactly what the question asks for (a total, a difference, what is left, an amount for each, change owed, a number of days). Then solve in short numbered steps, one calculation per step, with the arithmetic written out. Use every relevant fact once. Put quantities in the same unit before combining them (lengths, times, weights, money, calendar days). Read relations carefully: twice as many, more than, less than, each, per, the rest, half of, and which amount a fraction or percent is taken of. Answers are almost always whole numbers; if you get a fraction or an odd decimal, re-read the problem and check each step. Finish with one last line of the form 'Answer: ' followed by the number only, written in digits with no commas, units, currency signs or words, and nothing after it.
prompts.massive: Reply with one label copied exactly from the list and nothing else: no explanation, no second label. First find the domain (device, app or service), then the action from the label's last part: query asks for information or status; set, createoradd, order, sendemail and post create, add, order or send; remove deletes or cancels. Reminders and appointments are calendar; wake-ups are alarm. Current time, date or time zones are datetime. Starting playback is a play label; asking about a song is music_query; liking or disliking is likeness; shuffle or repeat is settings. Light colour is lightchange; brighter or dimmer is lightup or lightdim. Smart plugs and sockets are wemo. Things happening or to do are events; places like restaurants or shops are locations. Reading a feed is social_query; posting or complaining publicly is social_post. Greetings alone are general_greet; chit-chat, opinions and odd personal or philosophical questions are general_quirky; world facts are qa_factoid.
prompts.scifact: Reply with exactly one word, SUPPORT, CONTRADICT or NOT_ENOUGH_INFO, and nothing else. Silently: find the claim's subject, the effect or relationship it asserts, and its direction. Look in the abstract, especially its results and conclusions, for a statement about that same subject and relationship. Treat synonyms, abbreviations, gene or protein aliases and spelling slips as the same thing, and accept findings from animal models or study populations as evidence. SUPPORT: the abstract states or clearly implies the claim; a claim of no effect is supported by a finding of no significant effect. CONTRADICT: the abstract reports the opposite direction, or no change where the claim asserts a change. NOT_ENOUGH_INFO: the abstract is only on a related topic, about a different molecule, measure, population or outcome, or it never tests the specific relationship claimed. Use only the abstract, not outside knowledge.
prompts.mbpp: Reply with one fenced Python code block (```python ... ```) and nothing else. Put any imports at the top of the block, then define the function and any helpers. Copy the function name exactly from the example test, including capital letters, and accept the same number and order of arguments, even ones you do not need, such as a length. The code is also run on hidden tests with other inputs, so solve the general task; never hard-code the example's values. Make the return value match the example's type and format exactly: list versus tuple, int versus float, True/False, a string with the same wording, case and spacing, and floats rounded to the number of decimals shown. Before writing, trace the example test through your logic by hand; if the description is ambiguous, choose the reading that makes the example pass. Use only the standard library. Do not include asserts, tests, print calls, input() or example usage.
prompts.arc: Reply with only the label of the one best option, a single letter (or number, if the options are numbered), with no option text, punctuation or explanation. Before answering, silently: identify the science idea being tested; note qualifiers such as best, most likely, least, not, first, or whether an inference or an observation is asked for; predict the answer yourself; then check each option and eliminate those that are false, that are true but do not answer this exact question, or that only restate what was seen. For an inference or explanation, pick the option giving the underlying scientific reason. For least or not questions, pick the option that does not fit. Prefer the standard school textbook answer and do not overthink unusual edge cases. Always choose exactly one option, even when unsure.
prompts.banking77: Reply with one label copied exactly from the list, keeping any capital letter or question mark, and nothing else. Decide two things. 1) The topic: card payment, top-up, transfer, cash withdrawal, currency exchange, the card itself (ordering, delivery, activation, PIN) or identity checks. 2) The situation: a how-to or general question, or a problem with a specific transaction. Status words matter: pending is still processing; declined is refused; failed did not go through; reverted or cancelled went through and was undone; not recognised means an unknown payment; fee or charge means charged extra. Asking how long something takes is a timing or delivery-estimate label; complaining it has not come is an arrival or not-received label. Money not yet showing after a top-up is pending top-up; after a bank transfer or deposit it is balance not updated. Asking how to do something differs from saying it failed. Prefer the most specific label (contactless, virtual, ATM) over a general one.
